JUDGMENT
This petition is filed u/s 166 of the M.V. Act seeking compensation for the death caused in a road traffic accident.

2. The facts leading to the filing of top noted petition are that on 03.08.2024 the deceased was traveling from Bangarpet SCCH-23 MVC.6672/2024 to Bengaluru in a car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-MC-6402, along with three friends and one Nischal @ Prajwal was driven the car at the time of accident.

On the way at about 2.50 a.m, when the said car reached in front of Rock Valley School, Near Chikkahasala Village, on Bangarpet - Kolar road, Kolar Taluk and District, the driver of the car drove it in a rash & negligent manner and while over taking an unknown vehicle, that was proceeding in front of the said car, he lost control over the vehicle and as a result of which the said car went off the road and on the footpath and dashed against a road side tree.
Consequent to which the deceased and others sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the said injuries on the spot.

Postmortem was conducted and corpse was handed over to the family members, who conducted funeral and other ceremonies and they have spent substantial amount towards medical expenses,
transportation of dead body and funeral obsequies.

Further it is alleged that at the time of accident the deceased was studying 4th year Final year Bachelor of Engineering at Reva University College,
Bengaluru.
It is alleged SCCH-23 MVC.6672/2024 that the deceased was bright student and he was best at his studies and sports.

Further the deceased had potential to earn more than Rs.1 lakh p.m,
initially after completion of his Engineering Course.
It is further submitted that because of death of deceased the petitioners have suffered both financially and emotionally.
It is contended that the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of the driver of car and as such both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence prayed to allow the petition.
3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.1, the respondent No.1 did not appear before this Tribunal.
Hence he placed exparte.
4. After service of notice, respondent No.2 appeared through it's counsel and filed written statement and contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.
The respondent No.2 admitting the issuance of insurance policy in respect of car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-MC-6402.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.
The petition is barred by limitation. Non- SCCH-23 MVC.6672/2024 compliance of sections 134(c), 158(6) of MV Act
is pleaded.

This respondent contended that the owner of the car not paid the additional premium to cover the risk of Pavithra vs Ganta Hima Kumar on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76701032/
2 the occupants of the car.

It is further contended that the charge sheeted driver / Prajwal (deceased)
who was driving the car without having a proper lookout at the vehicular movement on the public place by consuming alcohol and the the said driver was solely responsible for the occurrence of the accident.
Further the occupants of the car namely deceased Harshavardhan, Basavanagowda and all the persons in the car had consumed alcohol, all of them violated the terms and conditions of the policy.

This goes to show that the driver was driving the car in the intoxication condition and thereby the police have filed charge sheet against him for the offences punishable u/s 281, 106(1) of BNS and u/s 185 (A) of M.V.Act.
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the insured vehicle did not possess valid & effective DL.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver.
On account of willful breach of the terms & SCCH-23 MVC.6672/2024 conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petitions.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petitions.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased ?
2) Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 03.08.2024 at about 2.50 a.m.,
in front of Rock Valley School, near Chikkahasala Village, on Bangarpet - Kolar road,
Kolar Taluk and District, due to actionable negligence of the driver of car bearing Reg. No.KA-51-MC-6402 ?

3) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed ? If so, at what rate and from whom ?
4) What order or award ?
6. Petitioner No.2 examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's.P1 to 14 were marked on behalf of the petitioners.
In order to prove its defence, the Deputy Legal Manager of respondent No.2 insurance company examined as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1 to 3 documents.
Heard counsel for the petitioners and respondent No.2 on merits.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

8. This tribunal answers to the above issues are as follows :-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative Pavithra vs Ganta Hima Kumar on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76701032/
3  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.4 : As per final order for the  following :
 REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.2 : The evidence of PW.1 and police documents placed on record indicate that on 03.08.2024 an accident had taken place and on the same day a complaint was lodged against the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-MC-6402.

entities.text: Affirmative Pavithra vs Ganta Hima Kumar on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Based on the complaint, the jurisdictional police registered the FIR and took-up investigation.
It is pertinent to note that in the accident except the car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-MC-6402 no other vehicle is involved.
Negligence means failure to exercise required degree of care which is expected of a prudent driver.
Negligence is not always a question of direct evidence.
It is an inference to be drawn from the proved facts.
When a motor SCCH-23 MVC.6672/2024 vehicle is being driven with reasonable care, it would ordinarily not meet with an accident.
Therefore the rule of res-ipsa loquitor as rule of evidence may be invoked in motor accident cases with greater frequency than in ordinary civil suits.

The very fact that the driver of car while over taking an unknown vehicle that was proceeding in front of the said car, he lost control over his vehicle and as a result the said car went off the road and on to the footpath and dashed against a road side tree indicates negligence on the part of its driver.
Hence the jurisdictional police have also filed charge sheet against him for the offences punishable u/s 281, 106(1) of BNS and u/s 185 (A) of M.V.Act.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
10. The respondent No.1 failed to appear despite due service of notice of the petition upon him.
Accordingly an adverse inference could be drawn against him that he has impliedly admitted the petition averments.
Though the insurance company denied the cause of the accident, it has not let in any cogent evidence to prove its defence.
No doubt, the SCCH-23 MVC.6672/2024 official of the insurance company was examined as RW.1.
But her evidence is no way helpful to prove the defence of insurance company.
Because she is not an eye-witness to the accident and her evidence is not supported by any document or any independent witness.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Therefore based on oral and documentary evidence, I hold that actionable negligence on the part of the driver of car is proved.

11. In addenda, in a claim for compensation u/s 166 of M.V Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in 'MANGALA RAM VS. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY reported in (2018) 5 SCC 656.

entities.text: MANGALA RAM VS. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY reported in (2018) 5 SCC 656
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As such, I answer issue No.2 in the Affirmative.
12. ISSUE No.1 :

The petitioner No.2 filed affidavit in lieu of his chief-examination and deposed that petitioner No.1 and 2 SCCH-23 MVC.6672/2024 are the parents and petitioner No.3 is the younger sister of the deceased.
The Aadhaar cards of the petitioners and deceased and contents of the police papers reflect the aforesaid relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.

Since the evidence led by PW.1 is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants,
hence, I hold that the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased.
Accordingly, this Tribunal answers issue No.1 In the Affirmative.

4 13. ISSUE No.3:
In this case the petitioners have claimed the compensation of Rs.1 crore due to the death of deceased in the road traffic accident.

It is the specific defence urged by the petitioners counsel that the deceased was aged about 21 years, and he was studying 4th year Final year Bachelor of Engineering at Reva University College, Bengaluru.
It is alleged that the deceased was bright student and he was best at his studies and sports.
Further the deceased had potential to earn more than Rs.1,00,000/- p.m, initially after completion of his Engineering Course.
Due to the accidental death the petitioners were put SCCH-23 MVC.6672/2024 into great mental shock and agony.
It is also vociferously urged that in twinkling of eye whole family structure of the family of the petitioners is demolished by this ill-fated accident.
14. The petitioners in order to prove the educational expertise of the deceased has got marked Ex.P8 SSLC Marks card, Ex.P.9 PUC Marks card and Ex.P.10 B.Tech Marks card from 1 to 6 semester.

The learned counsel for the petitioners have relied on the decision of Honble Supreme Court reported in 2020 0 Supreme (Kar) 1335 in the case of Sherly Jeevan V/s R.K.S. Infra Tech Pvt. Ltd., wherein the deceased in the above cited decision was an engineering student and the Hon'ble Court had considered his income at Rs.30,000/- p.m. and granted compensation.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

Based on the said decision it was strenuously canvassed by the learned counsel for the petitioner the minimum of Rs.30,000/-
p.m income may be taken.

15. It is relevant to relying on the decision of the Hon'ble High Court reported in 2020 0 Supreme(Kar) 104 (Shri Mallikarjun S/o. Yallappa Jogannavar and Ors. vs. Shri Umesh M. S/o.
Murthy K. and Ors.) wherein the deceased in SCCH-23 MVC.6672/2024 the above cited decision was an engineering student and the Hon'ble Court had considered his income at Rs.25,000/- p.m.
and granted compensation.

16. Further it is also relevant to relied on the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in (2015) 2 SCC 180 (Ashwinbhai Jayantilal Modi vs. Ramkaran Ramachandra Sharma and another) wherein for a MBBS student, the Court has taken the income as Rs.25,000/- p.m.
17.

entities.text: (2015) 2 SCC 180 (Ashwinbhai Jayantilal Modi vs. Ramkaran Ramachandra Sharma and another)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The pith and substance of these decisions it is clear that the deceased was pursuing B.E.
No doubt his studies might have improved during his degree days.
But the mere fact of deceased pursuing his BE, degree goes to show that he had bright future.
Therefore, Rs.25,000/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the deceased.

18. So far as the age of the deceased is concerned, the petitioners have produced the notarized copy of Aadhaar card of the deceased to show the age of the deceased as per Ex.P14, wherein the date of birth of deceased is shown as 28.07.2003. which indicates that he was aged (21 years 0 months 6 days) 21 SCCH-23 MVC.6672/2024 years on the date of accident.

Therefore the appropriate multiplier as per Sarla Verma's case for the said age group is '18'.
19.

As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others), if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospect has to taken into consideration while awarding compensation.

entities.text: 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Hon'ble Apex Court has provide the chart for age of the deceased and percentage for future Pavithra vs Ganta Hima Kumar on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76701032/
5 prospects in between below the age of 40 years 40%, 40 years to 50 years 25% and 50 to 60 years 10%.
The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and he died at the age of 21 years.
Therefore, in this case, 40% income has to be taken into consideration for future prospects.

Further as stated above that, as on the date of accident, deceased was aged about 21 years and as such, 40% is added to the income of the deceased, then it comes to Rs.35,000/- p.m.
(Rs.25,000/- + 10,000/- i.e., 40%).
SCCH-23 MVC.6672/2024 20.
Further as stated above that deceased was a bachelor
, as per the decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla verma V/s.
Delhi Transport Corporation

, the 50% of the income of the deceased shall be deducted towards her personal expenses as the deceased unmarried, thereby the 50% income of the deceased has to be deducted for her personal expenditure.

On such deduction,
the income of the deceased comes to Rs.17,500/- p.m. (Rs.35,000/- X 50/100).
21. The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.17,500/- p.m. and the multiplier "18" is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.37,80,000/- (Rs.17,500 X 12 X 18)

Considering the above facts,
I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.37,80,000/- under the head of loss of dependency.

22. In this case, petitioner No.1 & 2 are the parents of the deceased and as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioners are entitled SCCH-23 MVC.6672/2024 for filial consortium,
as the filial consortium is the right of the parents to compensation in the case of an accidental death of a child.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An accident leading to the death of a daughter causes great shock and agony to the parents and family of the deceased.
The greatest agony for a parent is to lose of their daughter during their lifetime.
Children are valued for their love, affection, companionship and their oral in the family unit.
Therefore, petitioner No.1 & 2 are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each under the head of Filial consortium.

23. Further, as law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex court in National Insurance company Vs Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to the estate, funeral expenses and consortium to be awarded.

entities.text: National Insurance company Vs Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence this Tribunal award Rs.18,150/- towards loss to estate and Rs.18,150/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years.

Compensation heads Compensation amount 1.
Towards loss of dependency Rs.37,80,000-00 SCCH-23 MVC.6672/2024 2.
Towards loss of Filial Consortium Rs. 80,000-00 to the petitioners No.1 & 2 3.

Towards loss to estate Rs. 18,150-00 Pavithra vs Ganta Hima Kumar on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76701032/
6 4.
Towards transportation of dead Rs. 18,150-00 body funeral and obsequies ceremony expenses Total Rs.38,96,300-00 25.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded, it would meet the ends of justice.
26. As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with respondent No.2 and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the driver of the offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
But if the charge sheet is perused, the driver of the offending vehicle was charge sheeted even for the offence punishable u/s 185(A) of IMV Act for his driving the vehicle under intoxication mind.

It is argued by the learned counsel for petitioners that there is no evidence to say the quantity of liquor consumed by the driver of offending vehicle so as to say that, he SCCH-23 MVC.6672/2024 has violated the rules by driving the vehicle under intoxication.

In order to prove the said same, the respondent No.2 insurance company examined its official as RW.1, she has produced Ex.R.3 being the FSL Report, wherein it is clearly stated that the quantity of alcohol consumed by the inmates of car as as follows :
Article No.1 (Prajwal @ Nischal) = 267.01 mg/100ml of blood Article No.3 (Basavanagouda) = 23.15mg/100 ml of blood Article No.5 (Harsha @Harshavardhan)
= 35.93mg/100ml of blood The drink and drive alcohol limit is a blood alcohol concentration of 0.03% or 30 mg of alcohol per 100 ml of blood.
Driving with a blood alcohol concentration exceeding this limit is illegal and it attracts imprisonment u/s 185 of the Motor vehicles Act 1988.

In the present case the blood alcohol concentration in the body of the driver of the offending vehicle was 267.01 m.g., which is exceeding the limit, hence only the investigating officer filed charge sheet against the driver even for the offence punishable u/s 185 of the Motor vehicles Act SCCH-23 MVC.6672/2024 27.

So far as the liability of paying compensation is concerned, it is true that all the documents pertaining to the offending vehicle was in force as on the date of accident but, as observed supra, the driver under the drunken state of mind drive the vehicle and caused for the accident.
28. The learned counsel for the petitioners has relied upon the decision of our Honble High Court of Karnataka reported in 2022 ACJ 650 between Rekha Devi and others V/s Mukesh Yadav and another.

sentences.text: 29. In the said case also all the documents pertaining to the offending vehicle was in force, but at the time of accident SCCH-23 MVC.6672/2024 the driver of the offending vehicle was under the Pavithra vs Ganta Hima Kumar on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76701032/
7 influence of alcohol.

The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has observed that the driving of vehicle under the influence of alcohol may be violation of an implied contract between insurer and insured,
but as far as third party is concerned the insurer cannot disown its liability to pay the compensation.
Section 147 and 149 of M.V. Act do not state that on that ground insurer can deny its liability to pay the compensation.

As per decision of Honble High Court of Madras, in 2025 ACJ 1925 between Branch Manager, SBI Gen.Ins.Co.Ltd., V/s Muthulakshmi and others held that : even after Amendment Act, 2019 the Tribunal is empowered to order insurance company to pay compensation and recover from the owner.

entities.text: Branch Manager, SBI Gen.Ins.Co.Ltd., V/s Muthulakshmi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore under such circumstances the insurer is liable to pay the compensation and it is at liberty to recover the same from the owner of the vehicle, since the owner has handed over the vehicle to a person who was driving the vehicle under the influence of alcohol,
contrary to provision of Section 185 of M.V. Act.

Further In MFA.No.4090 of 2016 (MV-I) decided on 03.07.2025 between The Oriental Ins. Co.
Ltd., V/s Sri.Pratik Kumar Tripathy and others.

entities.text:
Oriental Ins. Co.
Ltd., V/s Sri.Pratik Kumar Tripathy and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the similar set of facts has ordered for pay and recovery.
In the said case the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has referred many number of judgments of different High courts decided recently, wherein also pay and recovery was ordered.

Among them the Hon'ble High Court of Kerala in the case of Mohammed Rashid @ Rashid V/s Girivasan E.K. (MACA No.616/2018 decided on 30.01.2023 reported in 2023 live law (Kerala) 52 held that, in case of drink and drive the owner of the vehicle is liable to pay the compensation and the insurer shall pay the compensation to the third party and recover the same from the owner of the vehicle.

31. ISSUE NO.4 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
SCCH-23 MVC.6672/2024 ORDER

The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.38,96,300/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.

The respondent No.2 is hereby directed to pay the aforesaid award amount together with interest to the petitioner within two months from the date of this order, with liberty to recover the same from the insured/respondent No.1 in appropriate execution proceedings.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
Petitioner No.1 - 45% Petitioner No.2 - 45% Petitioner No.3 - 10% Out of the share amount of petitioners No.1 & 2 a sum equal to 25% each shall be deposited in their names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 5 years Pavithra vs Ganta Hima Kumar on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76701032/
8 and the SCCH-23 MVC.6672/2024 remaining 75% each shall be released to them through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioners are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on their deposit amount from time to time.

The share amount apportioned in the name of minor petitioner No.3 is ordered to be deposited in her name vide Fixed Deposit till she attains the age of majority, at any Nationalized/ Scheduled Bank as per the choice of the next friend/Natural guardian of the said minor petitioner.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased ?
2) Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 03.08.2024 at about 2.50 a.m.,
in front of Rock Valley School, near Chikkahasala Village, on Bangarpet - Kolar road,
Kolar Taluk and District, due to actionable negligence of the driver of car bearing Reg. No.KA-51-MC-6402 ?
3) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed ? If so, at what rate and from whom ?
4) What order or award ?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Negligence means failure to exercise required degree of care which is expected of a prudent driver.
Negligence is not always a question of direct evidence.
It is an inference to be drawn from the proved facts.
When a motor SCCH-23 MVC.6672/2024 vehicle is being driven with reasonable care, it would ordinarily not meet with an accident.
Therefore the rule of res-ipsa loquitor as rule of evidence may be invoked in motor accident cases with greater frequency than in ordinary civil suits.
The very fact that the driver of car while over taking an unknown vehicle that was proceeding in front of the said car, he lost control over his vehicle and as a result the said car went off the road and on to the footpath and dashed against a road side tree indicates negligence on the part of its driver.
Hence the jurisdictional police have also filed charge sheet against him for the offences punishable u/s 281, 106(1) of BNS and u/s 185 (A) of M.V.Act.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
10. The respondent No.1 failed to appear despite due service of notice of the petition upon him.
Accordingly an adverse inference could be drawn against him that he has impliedly admitted the petition averments.
Though the insurance company denied the cause of the accident, it has not let in any cogent evidence to prove its defence.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Therefore based on oral and documentary evidence, I hold that actionable negligence on the part of the driver of car is proved.
11. In addenda, in a claim for compensation u/s 166 of M.V Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in 'MANGALA RAM VS. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY reported in (2018) 5 SCC 656.
But the mere fact of deceased pursuing his BE, degree goes to show that he had bright future.
Therefore, Rs.25,000/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the deceased.
18. So far as the age of the deceased is concerned, the petitioners have produced the notarized copy of Aadhaar card of the deceased to show the age of the deceased as per Ex.P14, wherein the date of birth of deceased is shown as 28.07.2003. which indicates that he was aged (21 years 0 months 6 days) 21 SCCH-23 MVC.6672/2024 years on the date of accident.
Further the driver of the offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Driving with a blood alcohol concentration exceeding this limit is illegal and it attracts imprisonment u/s 185 of the Motor vehicles Act 1988.
In the present case the blood alcohol concentration in the body of the driver of the offending vehicle was 267.01 m.g., which is exceeding the limit, hence only the investigating officer filed charge sheet against the driver even for the offence punishable u/s 185 of the Motor vehicles Act SCCH-23 MVC.6672/2024 27.
So far as the liability of paying compensation is concerned, it is true that all the documents pertaining to the offending vehicle was in force as on the date of accident but, as observed supra, the driver under the drunken state of mind drive the vehicle and caused for the accident.
Further In MFA.No.4090 of 2016 (MV-I) decided on 03.07.2025 between The Oriental Ins. Co.
Ltd., V/s Sri.Pratik Kumar Tripathy and others.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Therefore, petitioner No.1 & 2 are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each under the head of Filial consortium.
Accordingly issue No.3 is answered as 'Partly in the affirmative'.
31. ISSUE NO.4 :
In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
SCCH-23 MVC.6672/2024 ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.38,96,300/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 is hereby directed to pay the aforesaid award amount together with interest to the petitioner within two months from the date of this order, with liberty to recover the same from the insured/respondent No.1 in appropriate execution proceedings.
On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
Petitioner No.1 - 45% Petitioner No.2 - 45% Petitioner No.3 - 10% Out of the share amount of petitioners No.1 & 2 a sum equal to 25% each shall be deposited in their names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 5 years Pavithra vs Ganta Hima Kumar on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76701032/
8 and the SCCH-23 MVC.6672/2024 remaining 75% each shall be released to them through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioners are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on their deposit amount from time to time.
The share amount apportioned in the name of minor petitioner No.3 is ordered to be deposited in her name vide Fixed Deposit till she attains the age of majority, at any Nationalized/ Scheduled Bank as per the choice of the next friend/Natural guardian of the said minor petitioner.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
